title: C3265A — Front seat climate control module [SCME] connector guide
introduction:
I use this reference as an address book for the seat-climate wiring: the drawing locates a cavity, and its matching table row explains the connection. Start with the connector identification table, find the printed cavity letter in the illustration, then read across that cavity’s assignment row. Keep the circuit identifier, color code, function and terminal information together; matching a color alone leaves most of the address missing.

The heater functions distinguish driver from passenger, cushion from backrest, and positive from negative connections. Those distinctions make this map useful when reading the associated wiring information. The identification and pigtail tables also connect the housing information with the listed service parts.

This is a connector-reading reference. Physical viewing direction, vehicle access, electrical test conditions and replacement instructions are outside its scope. The gauge convention and Size code are undefined here, so I retain those entries as recorded without converting them into wire-selection advice.

edits.why: I use the rounded housing outline and its left-side projection to recognize the drawing’s layout, then follow the printed cavity letters down the paired columns. Keep the lettering exactly as drawn rather than filling in skipped letters. The gray position corresponds to the assignment row with no circuit information; it is not an invitation to invent a missing connection.

The cavity label joins the illustration to the table. Read the whole matching row so the heater’s side, cushion or backrest location, and polarity stay attached to the correct circuit. The power and ground descriptions identify other connection functions. A RUN/START label describes the listed power function; it supplies no measurement or instruction to energize the connector.

The pigtail table links the kit entry with its service part and engineering shell. I keep those identifiers separate from the individual terminal part numbers in the assignment table: they describe different parts of the connector assembly. Use this section to understand the listed parts relationship; it does not teach connector replacement or establish interchangeability.
